body.x: Nolla design (CEO Sung-eun Jang, www.nolladesign.com) unveiled its highly efficient, mini solar charger, "SOLARADE," at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

SOLARADE is a highly efficient, 5-watt mini solar charger which can connect smart phones, tablet PCs, spare batteries and other devices via USB. The device is intended for IT/mobile equipment and comes with a sleek design. While SOLARADE is 20 percent smaller than other similar products currently on the market, it is 22 percent more energy efficient.

Among its ingenious features includes its solar recognition and angle repositioning mechanism which enables the device to reposition its solar panels to face the sun. With the SOLARADE a regular iPhone 5, for example, can fully recharge itself in just 2 hours. The device is also water-resistant.

Also set to be previewed are Nolla design’s "S-Clips" which connects to a diary to charge mobile phones via solar power. Unlike previous chargers which had to be equipped with a separate solar charger, this device allows one to charge simply by connecting with a diary. At 5-watt, it carries the same charging power capabilities as a standard charger.

A spokesperson for Nolla design said, “Though the CES 2015, we plan to introduce our highly efficient and portable solar chargers to the world. We aim to meet with many overseas buyers to form an export outlet for our products.”

Nolla design previously created the SOLARADE through the American-based crowdsource funding platform, Kickstarter, by securing $70,000 USD for its idea. It is currently developing other solar charging products for the market.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot.
